startup_sg_founder.problem_statement: Singapore SMEs lack affordable robotics automation for warehouse picking, forcing them to rely on manual labor that is increasingly hard to hire.
startup_sg_founder.solution: Acme Robotics builds a modular picking-arm system that integrates with existing warehouse racking with under a week of installation time.
startup_sg_founder.market_opportunity: The Southeast Asian warehouse automation market is projected to grow significantly as e-commerce fulfilment volumes rise and labor costs increase.
startup_sg_founder.founder_background: Alice Tan spent 6 years as a robotics lead at a logistics automation firm; Bob Lee previously ran commercial operations at a warehousing SaaS startup.
startup_sg_founder.use_of_funds: Funds will cover 2 additional engineering hires, tooling for a second prototype revision, and a 6-month pilot with two warehouse operators.

enterprise_development_grant.project_scope: Develop and productize the second-generation picking-arm controller software, adding multi-SKU recognition and a fleet-management dashboard so the system can be deployed across multiple warehouse sites simultaneously.
enterprise_development_grant.capability_area: Innovation & Productivity — automating warehouse picking workflows that today rely on manual labor, to raise throughput and lower unit fulfilment cost.
enterprise_development_grant.expected_outcomes: A 30% reduction in per-pick labor cost for pilot customers, support for at least 3 concurrent warehouse deployments, and a productized controller ready for commercial rollout within 12 months.
enterprise_development_grant.project_timeline: Months 1-3: controller architecture and multi-SKU recognition R&D. Months 4-8: fleet-management dashboard build and integration testing. Months 9-12: multi-site pilot deployment and commercial hardening.
enterprise_development_grant.use_of_funds: Funds will cover 2 additional engineering hires, tooling for a second prototype revision, and a 6-month pilot with two warehouse operators.
